Observation being separated from below for further discussion/debate:
https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/193753693

Observed on bluff face in natural botanical community, far removed from the gardens themselves:
https://www.kalmiagardens.org/explore-the-gardens/plant-preview/

Photographed on north facing slope. I did not have geotagging enabled on my camera and thus do not have GPS coordinates. However, I recall the location pretty well and should be fairly easy to relocate. As this is a T&E species, the location is auto obscured and I will not describe further publicly. (But can provide this data to SCDNR if needed.)

Observation was incidental, I was photographing the Galax urceolata. Others flagged the potential of Shortia galactifolia in the photo. I agree that the foliage beside the Galax is a different species and that it resembles Shortia, but have no experience with this very rare endemic. Thus I am only providing this initial identification to spark further discussion. I will default to whatever is determined by the experts.
